questions.question: A web application requests a video from a Sora 2 deployment and must return a response to the browser within two seconds. Which design is correct?

options.text: Use the images generation API and join the frames
options.why: Video generation uses the video API, not the images API.

options.text: Create the job, return the video ID to the browser, poll the job status, and download the content when the status is completed
options.why: Correct. Video generation is asynchronous: create, poll and download.

options.text: Hold the HTTP request open until the video is generated
options.why: Video generation takes much longer than a web request should wait.

options.text: Request a 4-second video so that the call returns immediately
options.why: Even short videos are generated as a job and are not returned in the create call.

questions.explanation: Sora 2 jobs are asynchronous. The application stores the video ID, checks the status and downloads the content after completion.

questions.question: A developer submits a request for a 1280x720 video and supplies a 720x1280 product image as the input reference. The request fails. What should the developer do?

options.text: Supply an input reference that has the same dimensions as the requested video
options.why: Correct. The input reference must match the video size exactly.

options.text: Convert the image to JPEG
options.why: The failure is caused by the size mismatch, not by the file format.

options.text: Deploy the model with the Standard deployment type
options.why: The deployment type is not related to the reference image size.

options.text: Change the duration to 12 seconds
options.why: Duration does not affect the size validation of the reference image.

questions.explanation: The input reference image must have the same width and height as the requested video.

questions.question: A request to Sora 2 that includes a team photo as the input reference returns a 400 error. The photo shows five employees. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The photo contains human faces, which are rejected as input images
options.why: Correct. Input images with human faces are rejected by Sora 2.

options.text: The video duration was set to 8 seconds
options.why: Eight seconds is a supported duration.

options.text: The prompt did not specify a camera movement
options.why: A camera movement is optional and does not cause a 400 error.

options.text: The photo has more than four megapixels
options.why: No such limit applies to the reference image in this scenario.

questions.explanation: Sora 2 rejects input images that contain human faces. Use a product or scene image as the reference instead.

questions.question: A video generated by Sora 2 is nearly correct, but the lighting must change from morning to sunset. All other content must stay as it is. Which approach minimizes the change to the rest of the video?

options.text: Delete the video and request it again with the same prompt
options.why: The same prompt can produce a different video.

options.text: Increase the video size to 1280x720
options.why: A larger size does not edit the lighting.

options.text: Remix the completed video with a prompt that describes the single lighting change
options.why: Correct. Remix starts from a completed video and a focused prompt keeps the rest stable.

options.text: Generate a new video with a longer prompt
options.why: A new job can change every element of the video.

questions.explanation: Remix applies a short change to a completed video, referenced by its ID. One clear change preserves most of the original.

questions.question: Which values are valid for the duration of a Sora 2 video request?

options.text: 4, 8 or 12 seconds
options.why: Correct. These are the supported durations.

options.text: 5, 10 or 15 seconds
options.why: These values are not supported.

options.text: Any whole number from 1 to 60 seconds
options.why: The service accepts only specific durations.

options.text: 30 or 60 seconds
options.why: Videos are limited to 12 seconds in a request.

questions.explanation: Sora 2 accepts 4, 8 or 12 seconds and the sizes 720x1280 or 1280x720. The model is in preview, so confirm the limits on Microsoft Learn.
